newsitem.title: GERMANY: Adidas plans office on former U.S. military base.
newsitem.headline: Adidas plans office on former U.S. military base.

text.p: Adidas AG said Tuesday it will stay in Germany and build a new headquarters on a former American military base close to the Bavarian town where Adi Dassler the sportswear group was founded in 1920.
The new headquarters will be built on a former base called "Herzo Base" that was left vacant when the United States reduced its forces in Europe after the end of the Cold War.
Adidas said its existing corporate headquarters, a rambling complex of buildings that includes a former villa belonging to founder Adi Dassler, was too small for its growing work force.

The news put an end to speculation that Adidas, led by Frenchman Robert Louis-Dreyfus, might move its headquarters out of the village of Herzogenaurach, or even leave Germany. Louis-Dreyfus is credited with saving Adidas from extinction in the early 1990s.
Adidas said it was in talks with the town of Herzogenaurch and a local real estate company to acquire the land. The new office is expected to be completed by the year 2000.
